pathway.title: SM Energy Co — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 2,940 million, made up of USD 442 million of cash and USD 2,498 million of undrawn commitments, is 47.6% of net debt, and no senior note falls due before July 2028. Only 40.4% of principal falls in 2028 to 2030 and 59.6% falls in 2031 to 2034, so a price fall has time to work through cash flow before bonds must be refinanced. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; calculation C16; calculation C13; calculation C15

Cash generation covers investment and leaves room to reduce debt, which is why the profile is improving: net debt at carrying value fell from USD 7,527 million at 31 March 2026 to USD 6,416 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 6,172 million at 30 September 2026. In the nine months to 30 September 2026 operating cash flow of USD 2,865 million funded capital expenditure of USD 2,020 million and left free cash flow of USD 845 million, or USD 492 million after stockholder payments. Adjusted EBITDAX covered cash interest paid 9.18x in the third quarter and 11.23x over the nine months, and covered it 5.13x after capital expenditure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Leverage cannot be measured on a comparable basis, which is a gap in the evidence more than a proven weakness. Net debt to reported EBITDA was 1.06x at the end of FY2025 for SM Energy alone, a figure that excludes the 2026 merger and sale, for which pro forma net leverage is not established, and the company states a target of low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026. Two proxies bracket the position without measuring it: four times third-quarter Adjusted EBITDAX gives 1.12x on the company's net debt, and a mechanical twelve-month sum that mixes pre- and post-merger periods gives 1.42x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C4

Price exposure is high and hedging has so far cost cash. Oil was 88.1% of production revenue in the nine months to 30 September 2026, hedge settlement losses of USD 457 million took 7.9% of revenue, and Adjusted EBITDAX margin was 64.2% against 72.1% before those losses and 67.7% on the same basis for FY2025. Operations improved before hedging because oil prices rose, and hedges gave much of the gain back; in a price fall the same contracts would pay. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10

Cost and capex flexibility are adequate rather than strong. Capital expenditure is discretionary: management plans about USD 2,750 million for 2026 and runs six rigs in the Permian Basin and one each in the DJ Basin and South Texas. Lease operating expense was USD 7.02 per BOE in the third quarter as mix shifted to higher-cost acquired assets, and the split between maintenance and growth capital is not disclosed, so the spending that could be cut without lowering volumes is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial policy is the main judgement. The Business & governance review rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: debt was reduced with asset-sale proceeds and cash flow, yet stockholder payments took 41.8% of free cash flow and the debt documents that cap such payments are not supplied. Integration looks largely complete on management's account, with about USD 400 million of run-rate synergies actioned, but oil guidance was trimmed and takeaway limits in the Uinta Basin persist. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3

runs.text: Liquidity and a late maturity wall are the first strength. Liquidity of USD 2,940 million against no bond until July 2028 means a price shock must persist for many quarters before refinancing pressure arises, which lowers near-term default risk. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16

Free cash flow after capital expenditure is the second strength. USD 845 million in nine months, with discretionary capital, lets the company reduce debt or return cash, and management has used it for both; the evidence supports lower loss severity only if returns do not outrun debt reduction. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11

Scale across four areas is the third strength. Production of 433.1 MBOE per day from the Permian, DJ, South Texas and Uinta areas spreads operating risk, though revenue stays tied to the oil price. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

Unmeasured combined leverage is the first weakness. Net debt of USD 6,172 million has no comparable earnings denominator, so creditors cannot confirm the company's low one-times target and must rely on proxies of 1.12x and 1.42x that bracket but do not measure it. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

Oil and hedge exposure is the second weakness. Oil is 88.1% of revenue and hedge settlements cost USD 457 million in nine months, so a price rise helps creditors less than shareholders and a fall exposes unhedged volumes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8

Stockholder-return policy with unseen limits is the third weakness. Stockholder payments of USD 353 million in nine months and USD 323 million of repurchase authority remain while net debt is above target, and the documents that cap them are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: SM Energy completed its merger with Civitas Resources, Inc. on 30 January 2026, under a merger agreement signed on 2 November 2025. Each Civitas share became 1.45 SM Energy shares, about 124 million shares were issued, equal to 52 percent of the enlarged share count, and total consideration was USD 2,664 million: cash of USD 226 million, shares of USD 2,409 million and replacement awards of USD 29 million. The company also assumed about USD 4.9 billion of Civitas senior notes at fair value of USD 5,090 million and repaid the Civitas revolver for USD 201 million. The purchase price allocation is preliminary. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

The same day the Credit Agreement was amended to permit the assumed notes, add the Civitas subsidiaries as guarantors, raise commitments from USD 2,000 million to USD 2,500 million and the borrowing base from USD 3,000 million to USD 5,000 million, and extend elected commitments to 2031; it also changed financial covenant definitions that are not printed. New debt in 2026 was one issue: USD 1,000 million of 6.625% senior notes due 2034, issued on 9 March 2026 at par for net proceeds of USD 984 million, used mainly to repurchase USD 894 million of higher-coupon 2028 Civitas notes. USD 1,236 million of 2026 and 2027 notes were then redeemed at par, leaving no senior note maturity until mid-2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; calculation C14; calculation C15

The South Texas assets of about 61,000 net acres were sold to Caturus Energy, LLC under an agreement of 17 February 2026 at a price of USD 950 million, closing on 30 April 2026. A final post-closing settlement after 30 September 2026, with its day not stated, brought net cash proceeds to USD 894 million and the final gain to USD 260 million. After the quarter end the lenders also reaffirmed the borrowing base and commitments, with the next redetermination on 1 April 2027. Both events fall after the balance-sheet date and are not blended into period figures. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 6,172 million at 30 September 2026 cannot be set against a comparable twelve-month EBITDA, so creditors must judge leverage from net debt, liquidity and the maturity wall rather than from a ratio. The January 2026 Civitas merger and the April 2026 South Texas sale mean no reported period before the third quarter of 2026 describes the company as it now stands.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At carrying value the company owed USD 6,614 million, all of it Senior Notes, with nothing drawn on the revolver and USD 2,940 million of cash and undrawn commitments; on the company's own principal definition net debt was USD 6,014 million. In FY2025, before the merger, net debt was 1.06x reported EBITDA and 1.04x Adjusted EBITDAX. No Senior Note matures before July 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Before the merger leverage was low and falling. Net debt fell from USD 2,777 million at the end of FY2024 to USD 2,347 million at the end of FY2025 while reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,916 million to USD 2,210 million, so net leverage eased from 1.45x to 1.06x. The merger then lifted net debt to USD 7,527 million at 31 March 2026, and South Texas sale proceeds of USD 889 million and cash generated above capital spending brought it down to USD 6,416 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 6,172 million at 30 September 2026.

A twelve-month window would join the fourth quarter of 2025, when SM Energy stood alone, to nine months in which Civitas appears only from 30 January 2026 and the South Texas assets only until 30 April 2026. The pieces describe different companies, so leverage and interest cover are left as not calculable rather than estimated, and the arithmetic that mixes them is shown in the calculations and not used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost has stepped up. Cash interest paid rose from USD 88 million in FY2024 to USD 166 million in FY2025, which cut reported EBITDA cover from 21.77x to 13.31x, and cash interest for the nine months of 2026 reached USD 331 million against USD 165 million a year earlier because most of the assumed Civitas notes carry higher coupons than the notes SM Energy had issued itself. The weighted-average interest rate was 7.6% in the third quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covered investment in the nine months to 30 September 2026. Operating cash flow of USD 2,865 million funded capital expenditure of USD 2,020 million and left free cash flow of USD 845 million, or 22.7% of Adjusted EBITDAX, after a working-capital outflow of USD 210 million and hedge settlement losses of USD 457 million. Capital spending fell from 45.8% of production revenue in FY2025 to 34.9% because revenue grew faster than spending, and the company places USD 227 million of one-time integration and divested-asset cash costs inside these figures, so underlying conversion is somewhat better than reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and no bond falls due soon. It was USD 2,940 million at 30 September 2026: USD 442 million of cash and USD 2,498 million of undrawn commitments after USD 2 million of letters of credit. The USD 5,000 million borrowing base is double the USD 2,500 million of commitments, so commitments set the limit, and the lenders reaffirmed both after the quarter end. Elected commitments mature in 2031; the maturity of the other commitments, and whether the October 2025 springing-maturity clause survives the January 2026 amendment, are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The maturity wall starts late and is spread out. No Senior Note falls due before July 2028, when USD 856 million matures, and the rest of the USD 6,456 million principal falls in 2029 to 2034, never more than USD 1,350 million in one year. The revolver is the only secured claim and is undrawn; all eight note series are unsecured, rank equally and carry the subsidiary guarantees that support the credit agreement, so any revolver drawing would rank ahead of the notes against the secured properties.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt are mostly operating. Asset retirement obligations were USD 426 million and derivative liabilities USD 565 million at 30 September 2026; delivery commitments carry undiscounted deficiency payments of up to USD 205 million if volumes are not delivered, and a drilling-footage agreement carries liquidated damages of up to USD 64 million. Operating lease liabilities were USD 138 million at the end of FY2025, the latest figure in the sources. The sources show no finance leases, factoring or supplier-finance programme.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Accounts payable and accrued expenses rose by USD 1,815 million to USD 2,505 million between year-end 2025 and 30 September 2026. This is operating float rather than debt, but it unwinds as invoices are paid and so draws on liquidity; the quarterly report does not break the balance down, so its composition is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three definitions change the numbers. Reported EBITDA is built from statement components because the company states none, and Adjusted EBITDAX exceeded it by USD 661 million in the nine months of 2026 after derivative losses, merger costs and the divestiture gain; debt is carried at USD 6,614 million, USD 158 million above principal because of fair-value premiums on the Civitas notes; and the covenant definitions were amended on 30 January 2026 with the amended text not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The case for a safer reading rests on earnings power rather than on any ratio the sources print. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDAX was USD 1,341 million on the post-sale asset base, and management states a target of low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026. The only arithmetic available, FY2025 plus nine months of 2026 less nine months of 2025, gives 1.42x on the company's net debt, but it omits Civitas earnings before 30 January 2026 and includes seven months of earnings from South Texas assets since sold, so it is shown for orientation and is not a measurement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage, interest cover and the pro forma net leverage after the final South Texas settlement are not calculable at 30 September 2026 because no comparable twelve-month EBITDA or cash interest exists after the merger and the sale; the pre-merger history of Civitas and any combined-company pro forma EBITDAX are not supplied. Severity High. A pro forma combined-company Adjusted EBITDAX and cash interest for twelve months, or four reported quarters after the sale, would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom is not measurable: the covenant definitions were amended on 30 January 2026, the amended text and the reported covenant ratio are not supplied, and only compliance at 30 September 2026 is stated. Severity High. The amended credit agreement and the compliance certificate would close it.

Severity Medium. The executed documents would close it.

Severity Low. The amended agreement would close it.

fields.value: - No balance sheet at 30 September 2025 is in the sources, so the nine-month 2025 column of the statements carries no balance-sheet figures and the period-end rows of the financials table are not supplied for it. Severity Low. The third-quarter 2025 report would close it.

Severity Low. No action needed.

fields.name: Quote

This corrects the Source readiness finding that the fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed at all: the first-quarter 2026 report prints a fourth-quarter 2025 column inside its Adjusted EBITDAX reconciliation (Adjusted EBITDAX USD 509 million), which this module uses, while the quarter's revenue and cash flows remain unprinted. Severity Low. The fourth-quarter 2025 release would close it.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

Severity Low. The settlement date would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tender offer consideration is USD 922 million in the second-quarter report and USD 924 million in the third, and the 2034 notes net proceeds are USD 985 million in the first-quarter report and USD 984 million in the third; the later amounts are used. Severity Low. No action needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by operating area is printed only for the third quarter and nine months, and the company reports one segment, so no area history for earlier periods is shown and no corporate or elimination amount is disclosed. Severity Low. Earlier area disclosures would close it.

fields.name: Quote

Severity Low. No action needed.

fields.value: SM Energy Co (issuer id sm), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the business, transaction, ownership, operating and governance facts that matter to a creditor, from the seven supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy's creditors face a widely held, merger-enlarged producer that has so far used asset sales and cash flow to reduce debt while also returning capital, so the main governance risk is how far unseen debt documents let that policy go. No sponsor or management fee appears in the sources, which is a strength.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Board composition, ownership concentration and restricted-payment capacity are not established because the proxy statement and the debt documents are not supplied. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, resting on behaviour alone: in the nine months to 30 September 2026 the company retired USD 2,160 million of notes and paid USD 353 million to stockholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is dispersed and no sponsor is evidenced, so extraction by an owner is not the risk. The company is a listed Delaware corporation, and former Civitas stockholders held 52 percent of its shares at the merger closing, but the sources name no large holder, and the proxy statement that would show holders, directors and related-party dealings is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management is deleveraging and returning capital at the same time, which makes shareholder policy the creditor's main watch point. Debt reduction came from asset sales and cash flow: the final South Texas proceeds of USD 894 million funded redemption of USD 819 million of 2026 notes, and cash flow funded the USD 417 million 2027 notes. Stockholder payments of USD 353 million were 41.8% of free cash flow after capital expenditure, and the base dividend was raised by 10 percent in February 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 tender offer was a creditor-neutral refinancing rather than a distribution. The company bought USD 894 million of its higher-coupon Civitas notes due 2028 at a premium to principal, paying USD 30 million of premium and fees, and funded it with new 2034 notes, so interest cost fell and the 2028 maturity shrank. The offer was open to all holders, and USD 456 million of those 2028 notes stayed outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Integration risk is moderate and mostly behind the company, but the evidence is management's own. The company says integration is substantially complete and that it has actioned about USD 400 million of run-rate synergies against an original target of USD 200 million, with one-time cash costs of USD 227 million inside nine-month adjusted free cash flow; oil volumes were held back by downtime and by takeaway limits in the Uinta Basin of about 4 MBbl per day that management expects to clear in early 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is an oil-weighted onshore producer in four areas, which ties creditor cash flow to the oil price. Oil was 88.1% of production revenue in the nine months to 30 September 2026, the Permian Basin supplied 51 percent of revenue, and one purchaser took 28% of FY2025 production revenue. Hedges are a net liability of USD 460 million and settlements cost USD 457 million in the nine months, so hedging cushions the price but has so far cost cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is good enough to monitor cash flow and debt but not to judge legal capacity. Results, reconciliations and debt tables are published each quarter, yet the covenant definitions were amended on 30 January 2026 without being printed, no covenant ratio is stated, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, raise debt or release liens is not established and the rating separates capacity from evidenced behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower risk level is that every documented action so far is creditor-aligned or neutral: no sponsor, no debt-funded distribution, USD 1,236 million of notes redeemed at par and a tender funded by cheaper debt, with stockholder payments at 12.3% of operating cash flow. The conduct evidence alone would support a Low rating. The rating stays Medium because distribution capacity under the debt documents, holder concentration and related-party dealings are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sight of the credit agreement and indentures showing tight restricted-payment limits, or leverage reaching the company's stated target of low one-times by year-end 2026, would move the rating to Low. A debt-funded acquisition, faster repurchases while net debt is still elevated, or a concentrated holder pressing for returns would move it to High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, independence, ownership concentration and related-party dealings are not established; this limits the Medium rating to conduct and means a concentrated holder or a related-party link would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement as amended and the indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, new debt and liens is not established; this stops the module separating what the company may do from what it has done, so no willingness conclusion is drawn from capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Synergy, integration and leverage-target statements are management language and are not audited; this means the cash-flow improvement they imply supports the view only once it shows in reported results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings say two rating agencies upgraded the company after the merger but name neither agency nor level, so no market-based check of the creditor-alignment reading is available.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy completed its merger with Civitas Resources, Inc. on 30 January 2026, under a merger agreement signed on 2 November 2025. Each Civitas share became 1.45 SM Energy shares, about 124 million shares were issued, equal to 52 percent of the enlarged share count, and total consideration was USD 2,664 million: cash of USD 226 million, shares of USD 2,409 million and replacement awards of USD 29 million. The company also assumed about USD 4.9 billion of Civitas senior notes at fair value of USD 5,090 million and repaid the Civitas revolver for USD 201 million. The purchase price allocation is preliminary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The same day the Credit Agreement was amended to permit the assumed notes, add the Civitas subsidiaries as guarantors, raise commitments from USD 2,000 million to USD 2,500 million and the borrowing base from USD 3,000 million to USD 5,000 million, and extend elected commitments to 2031; it also changed financial covenant definitions that are not printed. New debt in 2026 was one issue: USD 1,000 million of 6.625% senior notes due 2034, issued on 9 March 2026 at par for net proceeds of USD 984 million, used mainly to repurchase USD 894 million of higher-coupon 2028 Civitas notes. USD 1,236 million of 2026 and 2027 notes were then redeemed at par, leaving no senior note maturity until mid-2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The South Texas assets of about 61,000 net acres were sold to Caturus Energy, LLC under an agreement of 17 February 2026 at a price of USD 950 million, closing on 30 April 2026. A final post-closing settlement after 30 September 2026, with its day not stated, brought net cash proceeds to USD 894 million and the final gain to USD 260 million. After the quarter end the lenders also reaffirmed the borrowing base and commitments, with the next redetermination on 1 April 2027. Both events fall after the balance-sheet date and are not blended into period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, SM Energy presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the retirement of USD 2,160 million of notes alongside USD 353 million of stockholder payments in nine months 2026, which matters because cash paid out competes with debt reduction and implies slower deleveraging than the asset sales alone would allow. Countervailing evidence is the redemption of USD 1,236 million of notes at par and a tender funded by cheaper debt. Further analysis requires the credit agreement as amended, the indentures and the proxy statement. The governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Key gaps: debt documents, proxy statement, covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy Co (issuer id sm), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the issuer's fundamental credit profile from the seven supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving: USD 2,940 million of liquidity and no bond maturity before mid-2028 give creditors time, but earnings power on the enlarged balance sheet is unmeasured, so leverage rests on oil prices and management's deleveraging. Net debt was USD 6,172 million at 30 September 2026 at carrying value, or USD 6,167 million after the final South Texas settlement received after that date (day not stated); pro forma net leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside is a fall in oil prices while stockholder payments continue and net debt is still above the company's own low one-times target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 2,940 million, made up of USD 442 million of cash and USD 2,498 million of undrawn commitments, is 47.6% of net debt, and no senior note falls due before July 2028. Only 40.4% of principal falls in 2028 to 2030 and 59.6% falls in 2031 to 2034, so a price fall has time to work through cash flow before bonds must be refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; calculation C16; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covers investment and leaves room to reduce debt, which is why the profile is improving: net debt at carrying value fell from USD 7,527 million at 31 March 2026 to USD 6,416 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 6,172 million at 30 September 2026. In the nine months to 30 September 2026 operating cash flow of USD 2,865 million funded capital expenditure of USD 2,020 million and left free cash flow of USD 845 million, or USD 492 million after stockholder payments. Adjusted EBITDAX covered cash interest paid 9.18x in the third quarter and 11.23x over the nine months, and covered it 5.13x after capital expenditure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage cannot be measured on a comparable basis, which is a gap in the evidence more than a proven weakness. Net debt to reported EBITDA was 1.06x at the end of FY2025 for SM Energy alone, a figure that excludes the 2026 merger and sale, for which pro forma net leverage is not established, and the company states a target of low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026. Two proxies bracket the position without measuring it: four times third-quarter Adjusted EBITDAX gives 1.12x on the company's net debt, and a mechanical twelve-month sum that mixes pre- and post-merger periods gives 1.42x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price exposure is high and hedging has so far cost cash. Oil was 88.1% of production revenue in the nine months to 30 September 2026, hedge settlement losses of USD 457 million took 7.9% of revenue, and Adjusted EBITDAX margin was 64.2% against 72.1% before those losses and 67.7% on the same basis for FY2025. Operations improved before hedging because oil prices rose, and hedges gave much of the gain back; in a price fall the same contracts would pay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility are adequate rather than strong. Capital expenditure is discretionary: management plans about USD 2,750 million for 2026 and runs six rigs in the Permian Basin and one each in the DJ Basin and South Texas. Lease operating expense was USD 7.02 per BOE in the third quarter as mix shifted to higher-cost acquired assets, and the split between maintenance and growth capital is not disclosed, so the spending that could be cut without lowering volumes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main judgement. The Business & governance review rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: debt was reduced with asset-sale proceeds and cash flow, yet stockholder payments took 41.8% of free cash flow and the debt documents that cap such payments are not supplied. Integration looks largely complete on management's account, with about USD 400 million of run-rate synergies actioned, but oil guidance was trimmed and takeaway limits in the Uinta Basin persist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a weaker credit is that the improvement leans on high oil prices. Realized oil prices were USD 86.19 per barrel in the nine months against USD 65.28 a year earlier, the 12-month strip was USD 90.76 per barrel on 22 October 2026, and the company itself ties the rise to supply disruption. If prices revert, Adjusted EBITDAX falls while interest cost on the enlarged debt of USD 6,614 million at carrying value stays, and the hedge contracts for 2027 cover a part of volumes that is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four reported quarters after the sale showing net debt to Adjusted EBITDAX near the company's target would confirm an adequate-and-improving view and could support a stronger one. A fall of the oil price toward the hedge floors, drawings on the revolver, stockholder payments rising before the target is met, or a covenant definition tighter than the company's measure would move the view to weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No earnings history exists for the combined company on a comparable basis, so leverage and interest cover after the merger are bracketed by two proxies rather than measured; the adequate view of leverage is a judgement, not a calculation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Results fall in a period of elevated oil prices and no through-the-cycle figure is available, so the conclusions on margin and free cash flow hold only while prices stay near current levels, and the company's mid-cycle target cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Hedge coverage against forecast volumes is not stated, so the downside scenario describes the transmission qualitatively and the cash cost of a price fall is not sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity and recovery are outside this module and are not established in the sources, so the liquidity conclusion assumes the company's statement that it complies with its covenants and the revolver stays available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set or market quotes are supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with other leveraged oil and gas issuers; adequate is judged on the issuer's own evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy is an independent oil, gas and NGL producer in Texas, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah, with four operating areas after the Civitas merger of 30 January 2026. Third-quarter 2026 production was 433.1 MBOE per day, 222.7 MBOE per day of it in the Permian Basin, 119.4 MBOE per day in the DJ Basin, 46.3 MBOE per day in South Texas and 44.7 MBOE per day in the Uinta Basin, and oil was 84.1% of third-quarter production revenue. The business is a commodity price taker with no contracted revenue stream, so cash-flow visibility comes from hedges and capital discretion rather than customer contracts, and creditors depend on oil prices and operating execution across a larger but still oil-concentrated asset base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SM Energy is a listed Delaware corporation with no sponsor; former Civitas stockholders held 52 percent of its shares at the merger closing, and the sources name no controlling holder. The Credit Agreement and the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries, including those of Civitas, and the revolver is secured by mortgage liens on proved properties that also secure hedge obligations, so secured claims rank ahead of the unsecured notes against the same assets today. The proxy statement that would show holders and directors is not supplied, and the Business & governance review rates sponsor and governance risk Medium on conduct alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows volume and realized price: realized price per BOE was USD 54.23 in the third quarter and rose 19% over nine months on oil prices, while gas realizations were held back by regional differentials in the Permian and DJ basins. There is no pass-through or contract floor, one purchaser took 28% of FY2025 production revenue, and delivery commitments carry deficiency payments of up to USD 205 million. Revenue is therefore cyclical, price-taking and moderately concentrated, which makes the credit sensitive to the oil price and to the loss of one purchaser's payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Production costs are largely variable with price and volume: production taxes were USD 3.47 per BOE and lease operating expense USD 7.02 per BOE in the third quarter, and transportation USD 3.53 per BOE. Fixed costs sit in depreciation and general and administrative expense, and integration costs inflated nine-month general and administrative expense. Margin is resilient to volume loss through the variable taxes, but not to price: the 7.9% of revenue paid out on hedges shows how a price rise passes to hedge counterparties, and the mix shift toward higher-cost assets adds unit cost that synergies of about USD 400 million are meant to offset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 845 million in the nine months, 22.7% of Adjusted EBITDAX, and USD 411 million in the third quarter, with capital expenditure at 53.0% of third-quarter Adjusted EBITDAX. The company's own adjusted free cash flow was USD 884 million, and it carries USD 227 million of one-time integration and divested-asset cash costs. Cash taxes of USD 100 million to USD 120 million are guided for 2026 and the split between maintenance and growth capital is not disclosed. Conversion is adequate and capital is discretionary, so capex flexibility over the 2028 to 2034 maturity wall is real but unsized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is price rivalry among producers, so SM Energy cannot defend margin by price and relies on cost and basin quality. Buyer power is moderate: there are numerous purchasers in each area, but one took 28% of FY2025 production revenue. Supplier power is rising: management expects service-cost inflation, and capital guidance was held at about USD 2,750 million only through synergies and efficiency. New entrants and substitutes are not credit drivers over the 12 to 24 months that matter for the 2028 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and geopolitical factors do change the credit. Management links the higher oil prices of 2026 to Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, warns of tariff and inflation effects on oilfield costs, and says gas takeaway constraints in the Permian Basin and DJ Basin cut realized gas prices in the first half. A resolution of those conflicts would lower oil prices while service-cost inflation lingers, squeezing margin; this is the macro channel into the primary downside.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: liquidity of USD 2,940 million, no bond maturity before mid-2028, free cash flow of USD 845 million after capital expenditure in nine months, and a four-area asset base. Weaknesses: unmeasured combined leverage, 88.1% oil dependence, hedge settlement losses of USD 457 million, and stockholder payments of USD 353 million before the debt target is met. Opportunities: further asset sales and synergy delivery that lower net debt faster. Threats: oil price reversal, service-cost inflation, takeaway limits in the Uinta Basin and a tighter amended covenant definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and a late maturity wall are the first strength. Liquidity of USD 2,940 million against no bond until July 2028 means a price shock must persist for many quarters before refinancing pressure arises, which lowers near-term default risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow after capital expenditure is the second strength. USD 845 million in nine months, with discretionary capital, lets the company reduce debt or return cash, and management has used it for both; the evidence supports lower loss severity only if returns do not outrun debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale across four areas is the third strength. Production of 433.1 MBOE per day from the Permian, DJ, South Texas and Uinta areas spreads operating risk, though revenue stays tied to the oil price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unmeasured combined leverage is the first weakness. Net debt of USD 6,172 million has no comparable earnings denominator, so creditors cannot confirm the company's low one-times target and must rely on proxies of 1.12x and 1.42x that bracket but do not measure it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oil and hedge exposure is the second weakness. Oil is 88.1% of revenue and hedge settlements cost USD 457 million in nine months, so a price rise helps creditors less than shareholders and a fall exposes unhedged volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Stockholder-return policy with unseen limits is the third weakness. Stockholder payments of USD 353 million in nine months and USD 323 million of repurchase authority remain while net debt is above target, and the documents that cap them are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the company's guidance of fourth-quarter production of 435 to 445 MBOE per day and capital expenditure of about USD 610 million, a 12-month oil strip of USD 90.76 per barrel against USD 83.62 on 30 September 2026, and synergy delivery above target. The headwinds are hedge settlements at current prices, the Uinta Basin takeaway limit that management expects to clear in early 2027, and full-year oil guidance trimmed to 220 to 222 MBbl per day. Over three to five years the 8.9-year reserve life of the pre-merger company, the 2028 to 2034 maturities and the combined inventory decide whether debt can be reduced further without sacrificing volumes; no combined reserve figure is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit99111032026er.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is an oil price reversal as the supply disruption that management cites eases. Realized price per BOE falls first, and because production taxes fall with it while transportation, lease operating expense and general and administrative costs do not, Adjusted EBITDAX margin compresses beyond the price move; hedge contracts for 2027, including oil swaps of 12,542 MBbl at USD 68.70 per barrel and collars of 13,157 MBbl with a USD 63.93 floor, then pay out and cushion part of the loss, but their coverage against volumes is not stated. Free cash flow of USD 845 million over nine months would narrow and stockholder payments of USD 353 million would compete with debt reduction, so net debt stops falling. Management levers are capital expenditure, buybacks and the unused USD 2,498 million of commitments. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 because no bond is due before July 2028, the first observable trigger is quarterly free cash flow below the third-quarter figure with net debt flat, and, if the springing maturity clause still applies after the January 2026 amendment, its 91-day test begins to matter from April 2028 when availability is thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_sm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, SM Energy presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, a late maturity wall and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by unmeasured combined leverage, oil and hedge exposure and a stockholder-return policy whose limits are not visible. Cash-flow durability appears adequate while oil prices stay elevated and not fully assessable beyond that. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on oil prices, net debt reaching the company's target and the amended covenant terms when the 2028 notes approach. The primary downside path is an oil price reversal with continued stockholder payments. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, a comparable twelve-month combined EBITDAX and hedge coverage ratios. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: oil price reversal with leverage above target.
